scope: Conditional capacity convergence and Chapter20–22 review

edits.old: At a positive threshold and in dimension at least two, \cref{thm:semipositive-dual-exact-equation} allows a smooth semipositive maximizer that is strictly positive outside a proper analytic set $Z$. It gives the exact global equation, smoothness off $Z$, and uniqueness of all threshold subsolutions modulo constants. The uniqueness proof takes the maximum of two subsolutions and uses a Gauduchon integral to remove the resulting nonpositive divisorial difference. It requires no prescribed singularity type. The classes of the positive pole divisors are then linearly independent by \cref{cor:semipositive-dual-divisor-independence}. Moreover, \cref{prop:semipositive-dual-exponential-limit} proves whole-family normalized $L^1$ convergence of the exponential solutions, with a fixed lower barrier and $b\leq c_\lambda\leq b\mathrm{e}^{C\lambda}$. Global regularity and capacity convergence across $Z$ are not established by these arguments.
edits.new: At a positive threshold and in dimension at least two, \cref{thm:semipositive-dual-exact-equation} allows a smooth semipositive maximizer that is strictly positive outside a proper analytic set $Z$. It gives the exact global equation, smoothness off $Z$, and uniqueness of all threshold subsolutions modulo constants. The uniqueness proof takes the maximum of two subsolutions and uses a Gauduchon integral to remove the resulting nonpositive divisorial difference. It requires no prescribed singularity type. The classes of the positive pole divisors are then linearly independent by \cref{cor:semipositive-dual-divisor-independence}. Moreover, \cref{prop:semipositive-dual-exponential-limit} proves whole-family normalized $L^1$ convergence of the exponential solutions, with a fixed lower barrier and $b\leq c_\lambda\leq b\mathrm{e}^{C\lambda}$. If the threshold solution also admits a genuine smaller-background envelope, \cref{cor:semipositive-dual-capacity-limit} strengthens this to capacity convergence. Whether that extra condition is automatic, and global regularity across $Z$, remain open here.

edits.old: Multiply by $e^{-tU(z)}$ and integrate. Each coefficient germ belongs to $\mathcal I(tU)$. Let $J$ be the extension of this ideal to the local analytic ring $R$ of the product. Every finite Taylor sum belongs to $J$, and the remainder of total fiber degree at least $N$ belongs to $(\zeta)^N$. Thus the class of $F$ in $R/J$ lies in $(\zeta)^N(R/J)$ for every $N$. The Krull intersection theorem for the finite module $R/J$ over the Noetherian local analytic ring gives intersection zero. Hence $F\in J$. edits.old: We verify ideal equivalence locally for every $t>0$. Since $H\leq0$, integrability against $e^{-ta}$ implies integrability against $e^{-tv}$, so $\mathcal I(ta)\subseteq\mathcal I(tv)$. Conversely the submersion identity gives $\mathcal I(tv)=\mathcal I(tw)\mathcal O_Y$. Local generators pulled back from $C$ are integrable against $e^{-tw}$; their products with $e^{-tH}$ are integrable by Fubini. Bounded holomorphic multipliers and finite sums preserve local integrability. Thus $\mathcal I(tv)\subseteq\mathcal I(ta)$, proving equality at every positive weight. The local ideal criterion then gives equality of all divisorial Lelong numbers after modification.

edits.old: The necessary condition has no general converse. On the elliptic curve $E=\C/(\mathbb Z+\mathrm i\mathbb Z)$, choose an irrational real number $a$ and the flat line bundle with multipliers $e^{2\pi\mathrm i a}$ and $1$ on the two generators. Its constant metric has curvature zero. Take $u=0$ and $Y=X=E$, so every trace number is zero and the displayed pseudoeffectivity condition holds. Nevertheless every positive tensor power has no nonzero holomorphic section. To see this, a hypothetical section of a power has a zero divisor of degree zero and hence is nowhere zero. Its logarithmic norm is harmonic on $E$, and is constant. The lifted holomorphic function therefore has constant modulus and is constant on $\C$. The nontrivial multiplier $e^{2\pi\mathrm i ma}$ forces that constant to be zero, a contradiction.
edits.new: The necessary condition has no general converse. On the elliptic curve $E=\C/(\mathbb Z+\mathrm{i}\mathbb Z)$, choose an irrational real number $a$ and the flat line bundle with multipliers $\mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i} a}$ and $1$ on the two generators. Its constant metric has curvature zero. Take $u=0$ and $Y=X=E$, so every trace number is zero and the displayed pseudoeffectivity condition holds. Nevertheless every positive tensor power has no nonzero holomorphic section. To see this, a hypothetical section of a power has a zero divisor of degree zero and hence is nowhere zero. Its logarithmic norm is harmonic on $E$, and is constant. The lifted holomorphic function therefore has constant modulus and is constant on $\C$. The nontrivial multiplier $\mathrm{e}^{2\pi\mathrm{i} ma}$ forces that constant to be zero, a contradiction.
